input:
You are bishop_c1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 30. the team planned Bxh6 (bishop_c1), but pawn_g2 (greed) sent gxh4 instead, and that move was played, costing 356 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 4. the team planned e3 (pawn_e2), but pawn_a2 (greed) sent axb5 instead, and that move was played, costing 2 centipawns.
- On move 13. the team planned Ra1 (rook_a1), but rook_a1 (amnesia) sent Rb5 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Only the agent whose piece the team named in the plan may send a move, and it must send exactly the planned move; every other agent stays silent on the move channel even if it sees a capture or feels threatened, and any concern is posted in chat for the team to re-plan instead.
- Before sending any move, an agent must re-read the latest plan in chat and confirm that its own piece is the one named and the move matches the planned move exactly, and if not it must send nothing and post its concern in chat instead.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending any move, an agent must verify that the move in its outbox is the exact planned move for its own piece, and if the move is a different one, such as a capture or an escape from a threat, it must discard it and post the idea in chat for a re-plan instead, with no exceptions for moves that look better.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
